t: Arienzo, Collegiate Church of Sant'Andrea Apostolo
d: Baptisms 1672–1738 and 1761–1837; Marriages 1754–1900; Deaths 1733–1888. Reached through FamilySearch's handwriting-recognition full-text search. 2,059 baptism pages and 2,056 marriage and death pages were harvested — about 11.3 MB of machine transcription.
use: The spine of the archive. Every entry in the nine households comes from here.

d: The FamilySearch collection that carries the Arienzo baptism books.
use: Pasquale Falco's baptism of 24 October 1767, and the whole Matteo Falco household.

t: Italy, Campania, Deaths / Italy, Campania, Marriages
d: The companion full-text collections, carrying the Arienzo death and marriage series.
use: The marriage of Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci; the burials of Pasquale's children.

t: Italy, Benevento, Arcidiocesi di Benevento, Catholic Church Records, 1575–1908
d: Not yet worked. Covers Arpaia and Forchia.
use: Unread. Listed because it is the obvious next source for the Zampiello and Annecchino.

t: Italy, Caserta, Santa Maria Capua Vetere, Civil Registration (Tribunale), 1866–1929
d: The tribunal copies — births, marriages, deaths, banns, and the marriage supplements that quote earlier records.
use: Seventeen of the twenty-six citations carried over from the family tree.

d: From the introduction of civil registration in the Kingdom of Naples in 1809.
use: Carmine Antonio Falco's birth of 10 July 1850, which names his father Raffaele.
226 Zampiello records, all at Arpaia; 681 Annecchino records, of which 173 at Forchia.

d: Searched as a guest. Series J25 is the Brisbane naturalisation and immigration case files; K269 is incoming passenger lists.
use: That two Falco brothers married two Zampiello sisters; the arrival of 26 March 1964. The J25 files are paper only and unread.

t: Nudgee Cemetery, Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Brisbane
d: Searched through the Archdiocese's own portal at search.cemsearch.com.au — Nudgee is not a Brisbane City Council cemetery and is not in the council's grave search.
use: Five Falco burials with plot numbers, and the two corrections to the family record's death dates.

t: Arienzo: the comune and the Collegiata di Sant'Andrea
d: Town and diocesan histories, via Treccani, the Brisbane-independent Italian local-history sites and the Soprintendenza. Arienzo as Argentium on the ruins of Suessola; the Terra Murata of 1154; Sant'Andrea documented 1151 and collegiate from 1722.
use: The Places and Arienzo pages, and the town's Latin name Terra Argenti.

t: Alfonso Maria de' Liguori and the diocese of Sant'Agata de' Goti
d: Standard biography plus diocesan history. Bishop 1762–1775; second residence at Arienzo beside Sant'Andrea, now the Museo Alfonsiano; Arienzo passed to the diocese of Acerra in 1855.
use: The bishop next door — and the reason every Arienzo marriage dispensation runs through the Episcopalis Curia Sanctae Agathae Gothorum.
Falco: 46,749 bearers worldwide. Zampiello: about 123, of whom 37 in Italy.
About 7,826 Falco families in Italy; the regional split and the variant geography.

d: Ship histories for the Sydney and the Roma, the sister liners on the Europe–Australia migrant run from 1951.
use: The 1964 voyage, and the coincidence that two Zampiello sisters crossed on sister ships.

t: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione — Morti
d: One volume per year, 53–65 images each, no alphabetical index. Read linearly in full for 1834 (an_ua14336, 57 images), 1835 (an_ua14337) and 1836 (an_ua14338). Duplicate image bindings are intermittent and were mapped as encountered.
use: Yielded Pasquale Falco's death act of 1 October 1834 — the record that closed the line's oldest open question — plus six other Falco deaths and the identification of strada Camellara as the family's street.
